gifts.title: See which of our 30+ vendors are actually open now
gifts.for_complaint: Vendors/stalls closed or unpredictable hours, especially Sundays and evenings
gifts.deliverable: One public page (and a printable lobby/entrance sign) listing every current Midtown Global Market vendor with real day-by-day hours pulled from each vendor's own public Google Business listing, sorted so Sunday and evening gaps are visible before someone drives over — the exact complaint in 28 reviews spanning three years, none of which a single-vendor restaurant could ever generate.
gifts.inputs_needed: Current vendor roster (market's own directory page or a walk-through list from reviews) + each named vendor's public Google Business hours (individually searchable, no login) + the market's own posted overall hours for cross-check.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: It answers, in one glance, the exact question that produced their worst reviews for three straight years — 'will anything actually be open when I get there' — without needing one vendor's password or a single phone call.

gifts.title: A page proving it's safe to visit, not just saying so
gifts.for_complaint: Safety, homelessness, and drug/alcohol activity around entrances and outside the building
gifts.deliverable: A 'Getting Here Safely' page naming the specific well-lit ramp entrance on the east side (already referenced by visitors), the walking route from the METRO Blue Line Lake Street/Midtown Station, and the Minneapolis 3rd Precinct non-emergency line for anyone who feels unsafe — concrete, checkable facts standing in for the vague reassurance the current unanswered 1-star reviews are missing.
gifts.inputs_needed: METRO Transit stop location and public schedule (public GTFS/Metro Transit site), the building's ramp/entrance locations (OSM and Street View, public), Minneapolis 3rd Precinct non-emergency contact (public). Exact current security-desk staffing hours are not published anywhere public, so that one line ships as 'ask at the info desk' rather than a guess.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Four of the five most recent 1-star reviews cite exactly this fear and none got an answer — a page with a named route, a named station, and a real phone number replaces anxiety with a plan.

gifts.title: Straight answer: is parking here free or not?
gifts.for_complaint: Parking confusion: free vs. paid vs. validation, and lot size
gifts.deliverable: A one-page parking guide with a simple entrance map distinguishing the ramp (free with a vendor validation card, per multiple 5-star reviews describing the process) from the metered outdoor lot (reported at $2/hr), so a first-time visitor knows which lot to use and how to get validated before they pay something they didn't need to.
gifts.inputs_needed: Public satellite/street-view imagery of the two lots (Google Maps/OSM, public) plus the rate and validation-card process as independently documented across a dozen public reviews from 2023-2026.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Nine separate reviews over three years show visitors guessing whether they're about to get ticketed — this removes the guess before they pull in, and it's a question only a shared, multi-vendor lot generates.
